title: Experiences of a Lifetime
paragraphs: Kamila Seitkali has a list on the wall of her dormitory room. It is not a to-do list for university assignments. It is her 'bucket list' — a list of experiences she wants to have before she turns thirty. She has already crossed off five items. She has climbed a small mountain near Shymkent, tried skydiving, cooked a traditional Kazakh dinner for twenty people, learned to play three songs on the dombra, and visited the Charyn Canyon.

Kamila started the list when she was seventeen, after reading an article about the importance of collecting experiences rather than possessions. 'Things break and get old,' the article said. 'But memories stay with you forever.' This idea changed the way Kamila thinks about her free time. Instead of saving money for clothes or gadgets, she saves for trips and new activities.

Her most memorable experience so far has been the sky dive. She jumped from a plane at 4,000 metres above Kazakhstan's steppe. 'I have never felt so alive,' she told her classmates afterwards. 'For thirty seconds, I forgot everything — exams, deadlines, worries. There was just me and the sky.' Her friends thought she was crazy, but three of them have since tried it too.

Kamila has also had some experiences that did not go as planned. She has tried to learn Spanish twice, but she has not yet made much progress. She once attempted to cycle from Uralsk to the nearest village — 40 kilometres — but she gave up after 15 kilometres when her tyre burst. She laughs about these failures now. 'The ones that go wrong are often the best stories,' she says.

What is next on Kamila's bucket list? She has already planned her next adventure: a three-day hiking trip in the Altai Mountains with Amir, Zhibek, and Rustam. She has never been to the Altai region. She has already bought her hiking boots and packed her rucksack. The trip is next month. Kamila has counted: she has exactly sixteen experiences left to complete before she turns thirty.
